_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden pep). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. V2 REWRITE (2026-09-05): the entire tool was rebuilt to remove a fabricated measurement system that the old pep-v1 golden's own captured output demonstrates (energy_read/pleasure_vs_numbing language, nervous-system claims, quick_hits/medium_recharge/deep_reset categories, battery percentages, introvert/extrovert energy types, task-cost arithmetic, burnout-risk radar, and a debt-check 'prescription' action) — none of that exists in v2. DO NOT reintroduce it while chasing a golden diff. New schema per mode: generate={read,top_pick,other_options,from_your_history} (was energy_read/mood_note/time_note/transition_tip/pleasure_vs_numbing/menu.quick_hits+medium+deep+avoid); budget={read,protect,consider_next,postpone_or_drop,sequence,one_decision} (was capacity_status/total_cost/available/permissions/tomorrow_note — no more summing task 'cost' as literal arithmetic); forecast={week_shape,demanding_stretches,breathing_room,commitments_to_reconsider,from_your_history,one_move_now} (was current_battery/recharge_hours/introvert-extrovert drain multipliers — inputs are now demanding_factors checkboxes + starting_capacity, not an energy_type slider); disruption={situation,keep,lighten,pause,temporary_shape,unknowns,reassess_when,one_next_step} (was acknowledgment/survival_schedule/self_care_minimum — critically, disruption with a BLANK normal_routine must not invent a generic exercise/meal/hygiene/medication/sleep routine; it must list the gap under 'unknowns' instead, which the adapt-sick-day-sparse-input case exists specifically to guard). radar-checkin and radar-analyze (Patterns) now share ONE schema shape ({today,what_changed,possible_patterns,not_enough_to_tell,worth_watching,optional_next_step}) instead of radar-checkin's old ad hoc fields vs radar-analyze's separate overall_risk/time_until_concern/interventions shape — no green/yellow/orange/red status, no 'time until burnout' estimate. debt-check action REMOVED ENTIRELY (was prescription/debt_level/gentle_warning — all now-banned terms). Wire field names productivity/social_energy/physical_symptoms on radar-checkin/radar-analyze are DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED from v1 despite the UI relabeling 'Productivity' to 'Focus / getting things done' — preserves existing users' checkinLog history; do not rename these on a future pass without a migration. activityLog client-side cap raised from 6 to 100 (PF-25 exception, see src/tools/PEP.js). menu items no longer store category/effort/avg_rating/use_count/sensory_anchor — My Menu now computes timesTried/avgRating/energy ranges fresh from activityLog on every render (menuStats()), so a stale-cache class of bug is structurally gone. DO NOT reverse: the removal of battery/introvert-extrovert/burnout-radar/debt-check language; the disruption blank-routine guard; the unified Patterns schema; the productivity/social_energy field name preservation; the fresh-computed (not stored) menu stats.

input.context: Been staring at screens all day, doom-scrolling between meetings. A hike sounds awful right now.

output.read: You've been screen-bound all day and have very little in you right now — so the options below ask almost nothing of you and keep you away from another screen.

top_pick.activity: Sit or lie somewhere away from your screens with a drink or nothing at all, and just let the room be quiet for 15 minutes.
top_pick.why_it_fits: No setup, no screen, no decisions, and you're already home — it fits a 2/10 and a numb mood about as closely as anything can.
top_pick.first_step: Close or turn away from whatever screen you're on right now and find a spot to sit or lie down.
top_pick.done_when: When the 15 minutes are up, or whenever you feel like moving.

other_options.activity: Put something on to listen to — music, a podcast, an audiobook — with your eyes closed or looking at the ceiling.
other_options.why_it_fits: Audio only means no additional screen time, and you can do it lying completely still with zero setup beyond pressing play.
other_options.duration: As long as feels right up to 15 minutes.

other_options.activity: Make a simple drink — tea, water, whatever is easy — and just hold it for a bit.
other_options.why_it_fits: One short task with a clear end, no screen involved, and it gets you off the couch briefly without anything resembling a hike.
other_options.duration: 5 minutes or less to make it, then however long you want to sit with it.

output.read: You've rated your capacity at 3/10 and you're stressed, while your one required task is your most demanding item. That gap is worth acknowledging before deciding how to spend what you have.

protect.why: You marked it required, so I'd protect time for it unless you know it can move.
protect.make_it_easier: Rather than finishing it in one sitting, decide the smallest version of 'done' that satisfies the actual deadline — a complete draft, a specific section, or hitting send on what exists. Starting with one defined piece may be more workable than approaching the whole thing at once.

consider_next: Reply to 40 emails — if you do this at all today, consider whether you can reply to fewer: the ones that are actually time-sensitive, rather than all 40.

postpone_or_drop.reason: Optional, and doing it now adds demand on top of your required task without a clear payoff today.
Optional and higher demand than most of your other tasks. Nothing here suggests today is the right day to stack it in.

sequence: Quarterly report first — while your capacity is at its highest point of the day, whatever that is.
If something is left afterward and you want to use it, a reduced version of the email task.
output.one_decision: Define what 'finish' actually means for the quarterly report today — a specific, bounded output — so you know exactly what you are protecting capacity for.

input.what_helps: A quiet evening the night before

output.week_shape: The week is relatively open until Wednesday, which carries two back-to-back commitments — an all-day offsite followed immediately by a client dinner — with a major presentation the following morning. You are starting at 4/10 self-reported capacity.

demanding_stretches.what_makes_it_notable: The team offsite is all day with no early exit option, and the client dinner follows at 7pm the same day. You identified back-to-back commitments as especially demanding for you, and this is the clearest example of that pattern in the week you described.

The big presentation falls the morning after the longest day of the week, with no buffer between Wednesday evening and a 10am start. You identified hosting or leading as especially demanding, and presenting is a form of leading.

breathing_room.option: You mentioned a quiet evening the night before helps around busy days. Tuesday night is the evening before Wednesday's packed schedule — keeping it unscheduled or low-key is an option worth protecting.
These days appear unscheduled based on what you entered. Moving any flexible tasks or preparation work into these days could reduce what you are carrying into Wednesday.

breathing_room.when: Wednesday, between offsite end and dinner at 7pm
breathing_room.option: Depending on when the offsite ends, there may be a gap before 7pm. If there is, even a short unstructured window could give you a pause between the two commitments.

commitments_to_reconsider: The client dinner on Wednesday evening — you marked it as cannot leave early, but if there is any flexibility on whether to attend at all, it sits at the most compressed point of your week. Worth confirming whether attendance is truly required.
output.one_move_now: Protect Tuesday evening. It is the only quiet-evening slot before your most demanding stretch, and you named that pattern as something that helps you around busy days.

unknowns: Whether there are other obligations or constraints today.
